oneLine: Portable passkey approvals for AI publishing: verify the exact text, trusted approver and current consent on Monad before publication.
description:
A manager approves an AI-drafted announcement saying that support hours start on Monday. A downstream publisher changes Monday to Tuesday. The person is still signed in, but the published text no longer matches their decision. Orvena makes that difference verifiable across applications.

Orvena is a reusable approval protocol and TypeScript SDK for AI-assisted customer announcement and support publishing tools. A person reviews the exact text and confirms a fresh passkey assertion. Monad records a salted commitment; a portable JSON receipt travels with the draft. Another application independently checks the same UTF-8 bytes, an approver trusted by its own policy, the pinned deployment and current revocation state. Changed content fails. The owner can revoke with a new device confirmation, or approve a linked revision.

WHY MONAD: its native P256 precompile allows the contract to verify each WebAuthn approval and revocation. The gas sponsor submits the transaction but cannot forge the user's content decision. Shared onchain state lets a publisher verify without trusting the drafting application's database or contacting Orvena's API. Mera derives the enrollment account from passkey PRF output; the P256 credential key remains with the authenticator/provider. Users need no seed phrase, wallet extension or test MON.

WHAT IS BUILT: an immutable approval contract, portable receipt schema, origin-bound popup request SDK and independent verification SDK. The public approval app and publisher run on separate HTTPS origins. requestContentApproval gathers the user's decision; createApprovalReader checks chain state without login. Signatures bind action, owner, commitment or approval ID, parent, nonce, deadline, chain and contract; verification checks the registered key, RP/origin and user presence/verification. The approval contract has no admin, upgrade mechanism or fund custody.

EVIDENCE: live Monad testnet deployment (10143), 23 automated tests and two synthetic HTTP integration runs, each with 12 checks and four real testnet transactions. Separately, the submitted technical video records real Windows device passkey creation, approval and fresh revocation on the final HTTPS origin, changed-content rejection and receipt use in our publisher. A packed SDK was tested in a separate Node consumer without the Orvena API. Public transaction hashes and fixtures are linked from the README. Approval contract: 0x542ed99e33509dfecc7c4fc2d5293bf427cf91ba.

WHY DEVELOPERS WOULD INTEGRATE: one reusable consent format and current verification path across drafting and publishing systems, instead of assembling their own WebAuthn/P256, receipt transport and shared revocation infrastructure. The publisher must enforce the check at its authoritative publication boundary. It remains responsible for organizational authority.

Built by Efeberk Zorlukol, solo developer. The reference draft is prepared; no live AI model is connected. Approval proves key-authorized consent to exact bytes, not factual accuracy, authorship, model provenance, legal identity or personhood. Content and salt remain offchain; sharing a receipt shares its salt and does not provide zero-knowledge privacy. Revocation cannot recall prior disclosure. Verification is portable, while new passkey actions still require the original RP/domain and compatible provider. Our publisher is a project-owned integration; no independent customer adoption or external audit is claimed.
goToMarket:
FIRST CUSTOMER: developers of AI-assisted customer announcement and support publishing tools. The initial use case is a human-approved announcement moving from an AI drafting system into a separate publishing service. A changed or revoked version must fail the service's approval gate.

WHY ADOPT: integrate an existing popup request and current-state verification API instead of building WebAuthn/P256 validation, a portable receipt format, replay protection and cross-application revocation from scratch. Orvena supplies the consent primitive; the adopter keeps its existing user/role policy and publishing system. The live separate-origin publisher and installable SDK tarball provide a concrete integration starting point. The SDK is currently packaged from the public repository, not published on npm.

ACQUISITION PLAN: demonstrate the modified-text and revocation cases to three target developer teams, then invite a small pilot around one drafting-to-publishing workflow. Provide a copyable request example, backend verification guide and public testnet evidence. We have not yet completed external outreach or secured independent pilots, customers or adoption. Our own publisher demonstrates technical feasibility, not traction.

PILOT MEASUREMENT: time to first verified approval, approval completion rate, modified/revoked versions blocked, verification latency and sponsorship cost. Feedback will determine SDK changes, additional content types and organizational approver policy support. After a pilot, publish reproducible integration examples and results to support further developer adoption.

BUSINESS AND DELIVERY: potential paid offerings are managed sponsorship and integration support. Independent contract verification remains available without our hosted API. Before broader third-party release, complete repository-wide licensing and npm distribution; before production-scale sponsorship, add durable shared nonce coordination, distributed rate limits and abuse controls. Today's Vercel sponsor is a dedicated prefunded testnet account with a balance cap. These are next steps, not completed production capabilities.
judgeInstructions:
LIVE LINKS
Approval app: https://orvena-ashy.vercel.app/#app
Separate publisher: https://orvena-publisher.vercel.app
Source, setup and evidence: https://github.com/efeberk21/orvena
Quick walkthrough: https://github.com/efeberk21/orvena/blob/main/docs/JUDGES.md

OPTION A — VERIFY WITHOUT SIGNING IN
Open https://orvena-ashy.vercel.app/verify. Paste or import the receipt from examples/recorded-receipt.json in the repository. Enter the expected approver address 0xb0bE7f01e2280d9Fd669d3c45057591f552b8e10 and the exact text from examples/recorded-content.txt. Click Verify current approval. Expected result: revoked, because the user withdrew this recorded consent. Change Monday to Tuesday and verify again: content-mismatch. No passkey, test login, wallet or sponsor is required for these reads. This address is the independently pinned owner of our recorded public example, not a universal organizational authority.

OPTION B — APPROVE AND REVOKE YOUR OWN DRAFT
Use Chrome or Edge with a passkey authenticator/provider that supports WebAuthn PRF and user verification. Keep the stable HTTPS origin; localhost credentials do not transfer to this domain. Choose Create your passkey and confirm on your own device. If the provider lacks PRF, use Option A and the recorded demo, or switch to a compatible provider/device. No shared credentials are needed.

1. Review the prepared draft and approve with a fresh device confirmation. The dedicated sponsor registers the public key on first approval and pays testnet gas; no seed phrase, wallet extension, faucet or user-held MON is required.
2. Copy your account address as the trusted approver for this test and download the receipt. Check original text + receipt + expected address in the public verifier: valid. Change a word: content-mismatch. Whitespace also matters.
3. In the separately hosted publisher, use the same text, receipt and expected address, or request approval through its SDK popup. Permit the popup and complete the user review there. Its demo publication step requires a current valid check; changed text is blocked. A production service must enforce this on its authoritative backend.
4. Revoke from the approval app with another fresh device confirmation. Verify the original again: revoked. Historical records and previously shared content remain.

The repository's deployments/physical-passkey-10143.json links successful actual approval/revocation transactions from the recorded Windows device flow. Its receipt is already revoked. Synthetic P256 integration tests are labelled separately.

The draft is prepared and no live AI model is called. No independent adoption or external audit is claimed. Sponsorship is capped and may be exhausted; public verification reads Monad independently of the sponsor. No PIN, biometric data or private key should be shared.
